title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models

annotations.label: DreamerV3
annotations.short: The third generation of Dreamer, designed to learn across diverse domains with one fixed configuration.
annotations.details: DreamerV3 jointly trains a latent world model, critic, and actor. Its normalization, balancing, and transformed prediction losses are intended to remain stable across differing observation, reward, and action regimes.

annotations.label: World model
annotations.short: A learned model that compresses observations and predicts future latent states, rewards, and continuation.
annotations.details: Dreamer's world model is an RSSM trained from replayed experience. It supplies imagined trajectories on which the actor and critic learn without further environment interaction.

annotations.label: Critic
annotations.short: A network that predicts a distribution over returns for each model state.
annotations.details: The critic is parameterized by $\psi$ and trained on bootstrapped $\lambda$-return targets. Its expected prediction supplies values for bootstrapping and the actor's advantage estimate.

annotations.label: Actor
annotations.short: A policy network that samples actions to maximize return while retaining entropy for exploration.
annotations.details: The actor is parameterized by $\theta$ and trained on imagined model states using a REINFORCE surrogate. Percentile return normalization lets its fixed entropy coefficient work across reward scales.

annotations.label: RSSM
annotations.details: Dreamer uses an RSSM as its latent world model. Its deterministic state $h_t$ and stochastic state $z_t$ jointly summarize history and support fast latent predictions for imagination.

annotations.label: $x_t$
annotations.short: The sensory observation $x_t$ received at time $t$.
annotations.details: It can be an image or a vector depending on the domain. The encoder maps $x_t$ to $z_t$, and the decoder reconstructs it as $\hat{x}_t$ to keep the representation informative.

annotations.label: $z_t$
annotations.short: The sampled stochastic latent representation $z_t$ at time $t$.
annotations.details: The encoder samples $z_t$ from $q_\phi(z_t \mid h_t,x_t)$. Concatenated with $h_t$, it forms the model state used by prediction heads and behavior learning.

annotations.label: $h_t$
annotations.short: The deterministic recurrent state $h_t$ of the RSSM at time $t$.
annotations.details: The sequence model updates $h_t$ from $h_{t-1}$, $z_{t-1}$, and $a_{t-1}$. It carries temporal context needed to predict the next latent state.

annotations.label: $a_t$
annotations.short: The action $a_t$ selected at time $t$.
annotations.details: The actor samples $a_t$ from $\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)$. This current action determines the next transition in both imagined rollouts and environment interaction.

annotations.label: $a_{t-1}$
annotations.short: The previous action $a_{t-1}$, taken at time $t-1$.
annotations.details: The RSSM uses $a_{t-1}$ together with $h_{t-1}$ and $z_{t-1}$ to compute $h_t$. It is the one-step-lagged action, not the action $a_t$ selected at time $t$.

annotations.label: $s_t \doteq \{h_t,z_t\}$
annotations.short: The model state supplied to Dreamer's actor and critic.
annotations.details: The model state is $s_t \doteq \{h_t,z_t\}$, combining deterministic memory $h_t$ and stochastic representation $z_t$. The paper treats it as Markovian enough for value prediction and policy learning.

annotations.label: $r_t$
annotations.short: The scalar reward $r_t$ associated with time $t$.
annotations.details: The world model predicts $r_t$ for imagined states. It enters both the discounted return $R_t$ and recursive $\lambda$-return target $R_t^\lambda$.

annotations.label: $c_t$
annotations.short: The binary continuation flag $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ after time $t$.
annotations.details: $c_t$ gates future value in the $\lambda$-return recursion. Dreamer's continuation head predicts it from the latent model state.

annotations.label: $f_\phi(h_{t-1},z_{t-1},a_{t-1})$
annotations.short: The recurrent transition $f_\phi$ that computes $h_t$.
annotations.details: $f_\phi(h_{t-1},z_{t-1},a_{t-1})$ maps the preceding state and action to $h_t$. Its parameters belong to the world-model parameter set $\phi$.

annotations.label: $q_\phi(z_t \mid h_t,x_t)$
annotations.short: The encoder distribution $q_\phi(z_t \mid h_t,x_t)$ over the current latent state.
annotations.details: This posterior-like distribution conditions on recurrent context $h_t$ and observation $x_t$. Its samples train representations and provide targets for latent dynamics.

annotations.label: $\hat z_t$
annotations.short: A stochastic latent state predicted from recurrent context alone.
annotations.details: During imagination, $\hat z_t$ is sampled from $p_\phi(\hat z_t \mid h_t)$ without access to $x_t$. The dynamics loss aligns this predictor with encoder representations.

annotations.label: $\hat r_t$
annotations.short: The reward predicted by the world model at time t.
annotations.details: $\hat r_t$ is sampled from $p_\phi(\hat r_t \mid h_t,z_t)$. These predictions provide imagined rewards for actor–critic learning.

annotations.label: $\hat c_t$
annotations.short: The predicted episode-continuation flag.
annotations.details: $\hat c_t$ estimates whether an imagined trajectory remains nonterminal. It is trained by logistic regression and gates discounted future value.

annotations.label: $\hat x_t$
annotations.short: The decoder reconstruction $\hat x_t$ of observation $x_t$.
annotations.details: Reconstruction forces the latent state to preserve information about sensory inputs. Image and vector observations use different encoder/decoder architectures in the implementation.

annotations.label: $p_\phi(\hat z_t \mid h_t)$
annotations.short: $p_\phi(\hat z_t \mid h_t)$ predicts the next stochastic latent from recurrent state $h_t$.
annotations.details: This dynamics head generates $\hat z_t$ without observing $x_t$, enabling open-loop imagination. Its KL objective aligns it with encoder distribution $q_\phi(z_t \mid h_t,x_t)$.

annotations.label: $p_\phi(\hat r_t \mid h_t,z_t)$
annotations.short: $p_\phi(\hat r_t \mid h_t,z_t)$ predicts reward from the current latent model state.
annotations.details: This reward head supplies imagined rewards to the actor and critic. It is trained against replay reward $r_t$ using the symexp two-hot cross-entropy loss.

annotations.label: $p_\phi(\hat c_t \mid h_t,z_t)$
annotations.short: $p_\phi(\hat c_t \mid h_t,z_t)$ predicts whether an imagined episode continues.
annotations.details: This Bernoulli-style head estimates continuation $\hat c_t$ from the current model state. Its output gates discounted future value in imagined trajectories.

annotations.label: $p_\phi(\hat x_t \mid h_t,z_t)$
annotations.short: $p_\phi(\hat x_t \mid h_t,z_t)$ reconstructs the sensory observation.
annotations.details: The decoder head makes the latent state retain information about $x_t$. It uses convolutional decoding for images and an MLP for vector observations.

annotations.label: Straight-through gradient
annotations.short: A gradient estimator used to train through discrete latent samples.
annotations.details: If $p$ is the soft probability vector and $z$ its discrete sample, the straight-through construction $z_{\mathrm{st}}=\operatorname{sg}(z-p)+p$ equals $z$ in the forward pass but differentiates as $p$ in the backward pass. This lets Dreamer's encoder and predictor receive gradients through categorical samples.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L$
annotations.short: The total expected world-model training objective.
annotations.details: It sums $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{pred}}$, $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dyn}}$, and $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{rep}}$ across a sequence and averages under encoder samples $q_\phi$. Fixed $\beta$ coefficients balance the three terms.

annotations.label: $\beta_{\mathrm{pred}}$
annotations.short: $\beta_{\mathrm{pred}}=1$ weights the world model's prediction loss.
annotations.details: It scales $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{pred}}$, which trains observation reconstruction plus reward and continuation prediction. Its fixed value is part of DreamerV3's cross-domain configuration.

annotations.label: $\beta_{\mathrm{dyn}}$
annotations.short: $\beta_{\mathrm{dyn}}=1$ weights the latent dynamics loss.
annotations.details: It scales $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dyn}}$, whose gradient trains the dynamics predictor toward the stopped encoder distribution.

annotations.label: $\beta_{\mathrm{rep}}$
annotations.short: $\beta_{\mathrm{rep}}=0.1$ weights the representation regularizer.
annotations.details: It scales $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{rep}}$ more weakly than the other world-model terms, encouraging predictable latents without discarding task-relevant detail.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{pred}}$
annotations.short: The loss for reconstructing observations and predicting rewards and continuation.
annotations.details: It sums negative log likelihoods for $x_t$, $r_t$, and $c_t$ under their world-model heads. Its gradients train the decoder and reward/continuation predictors and shape useful representations.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dyn}}$
annotations.short: The KL loss that trains latent dynamics to predict encoder representations.
annotations.details: It compares stopped encoder target $q_\phi(z_t\mid h_t,x_t)$ with dynamics predictor $p_\phi(z_t\mid h_t)$ and applies a one-nat free-bits floor. Its gradients primarily update the predictor.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{rep}}$
annotations.short: The KL loss that makes encoder representations easier for the dynamics model to predict.
annotations.details: It reverses which side of the KL receives stop-gradient relative to $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ and also uses a one-nat floor. Its smaller global weight helps retain useful input detail.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{KL}$
annotations.details: Dreamer uses KL divergence to align $q_\phi(z_t\mid h_t,x_t)$ with $p_\phi(z_t\mid h_t)$. Separate stop-gradient placements split learning pressure between predictor and representation.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)$
annotations.details: In the two KL terms, $\sg(\cdot)$ chooses whether the encoder distribution or dynamics predictor acts as a fixed target. This balances representation and dynamics learning.

annotations.label: Free bits
annotations.short: A one-nat floor below which Dreamer's KL terms stop exerting optimization pressure.
annotations.details: The $\max(1,\mathrm{KL})$ construction prevents over-regularizing already compact latent representations. It allows up to one nat of KL divergence without optimization pressure, rather than enforcing the KL to equal one nat.

annotations.label: $-\ln p_\phi(x_t\mid z_t,h_t)$
annotations.short: $-\ln p_\phi(x_t\mid z_t,h_t)$ scores the reconstructed observation.
annotations.details: This term trains the decoder to assign high likelihood to replay observation $x_t$ given latent state $(h_t,z_t)$.

annotations.label: $-\ln p_\phi(r_t\mid z_t,h_t)$
annotations.short: $-\ln p_\phi(r_t\mid z_t,h_t)$ scores the observed reward.
annotations.details: This term trains the reward head to assign high likelihood to replay reward $r_t$ from latent model state $(h_t,z_t)$.

annotations.label: $-\ln p_\phi(c_t\mid z_t,h_t)$
annotations.short: $-\ln p_\phi(c_t\mid z_t,h_t)$ scores the observed continuation flag.
annotations.details: This logistic-regression term trains the continuation head on binary target $c_t$, distinguishing terminal from nonterminal transitions.

annotations.label: $R_t \doteq \sum_{\tau=0}^{\infty} \gamma^\tau r_{t+\tau}$
annotations.short: The infinite-horizon discounted sum of rewards from time t.
annotations.details: $R_t \doteq \sum_{\tau=0}^{\infty}\gamma^\tau r_{t+\tau}$ weights each future reward geometrically. The actor maximizes this quantity while the critic models its distribution.

annotations.label: $\gamma$
annotations.short: The temporal discount factor $\gamma=0.997$.
annotations.details: $\gamma^\tau$ reduces the contribution of distant rewards, and $\gamma c_t$ multiplies bootstrapped future value in the $\lambda$-return.

annotations.label: $\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)$
annotations.short: The actor's conditional action distribution.
annotations.details: $\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)$ maps latent state $s_t$ to a discrete or continuous action distribution. Actions are sampled from it during imagination and environment interaction.

annotations.label: $v_\psi(R_t\mid s_t)$
annotations.short: The critic's categorical distribution over returns conditioned on state.
annotations.details: $v_\psi(R_t\mid s_t)$ is categorical over exponentially spaced return bins. Its expectation is $v_t$, and its likelihood at $R_t^\lambda$ defines the critic loss.

annotations.label: $v_t$
annotations.short: The expected return $v_t$ read from the critic distribution at state $s_t$.
annotations.details: $v_t\doteq\operatorname E[v_\psi(\cdot\mid s_t)]$ bootstraps $\lambda$-returns and serves as the actor's baseline. Its units match return units.

annotations.label: Bootstrapped lambda-return
annotations.short: A target mixing reward $r_t$, critic value $v_t$, and recursively estimated future return.
annotations.details: $\lambda$ interpolates between one-step value bootstrapping and longer-horizon returns, incorporating rewards beyond Dreamer's finite imagination horizon.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L$
annotations.short: The critic's negative log-likelihood objective over lambda-return targets.
annotations.details: It sums $\log p_\psi(R_t^\lambda\mid s_t)$ over imagined states. Minimizing its negative fits the full categorical return distribution, not only its mean.

annotations.label: $\log p_\psi(R_t^\lambda\mid s_t)$
annotations.short: The critic log probability $\log p_\psi(R_t^\lambda\mid s_t)$ assigned to a $\lambda$-return target.
annotations.details: Here $p_\psi$ is the probability assigned by the categorical critic $v_\psi$ to the target return. The negative sum of these terms trains the critic, with continuous returns represented by soft labels over transformed categorical bins.

annotations.label: $R_t^\lambda$
annotations.short: The $\lambda$-return target $R_t^\lambda$ at time $t$.
annotations.details: $R_t^\lambda$ combines $r_t$ with a continuation-gated mixture of $v_t$ and $R_{t+1}^\lambda$. At horizon $T$, $R_T^\lambda\doteq v_T$.

annotations.label: $\lambda$
annotations.short: The mixing coefficient in the recursive lambda-return.
annotations.details: The factor $1-\lambda$ weights direct critic bootstrapping, while $\lambda$ weights $R_{t+1}^\lambda$. It controls target horizon and the bias–variance tradeoff.

annotations.label: Entropy regularization
annotations.short: An exploration bonus that favors less concentrated action distributions.
annotations.details: Dreamer's actor includes $\eta\,\mathrm H[\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)]$ as a bonus inside the negated return-maximization surrogate, so greater policy entropy lowers the minimized loss. Return normalization keeps this bonus meaningful across reward scales.

annotations.label: $\eta$
annotations.short: The fixed policy-entropy coefficient $\eta=3\times10^{-4}$.
annotations.details: $\eta$ controls exploration relative to the return-seeking term. Percentile normalization allows one value to be reused across domains.

annotations.label: $S$
annotations.short: A robust running scale estimate $S$ for $\lambda$-returns.
annotations.details: $S$ is an EMA of the 95th-minus-5th percentile range. Dividing by $\max(1,S)$ scales down large advantages without amplifying small sparse-reward signals.

annotations.label: REINFORCE estimator
annotations.details: Dreamer weights each sampled action's log probability by a stopped-gradient normalized advantage and uses this estimator for both discrete and continuous actions.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L$
annotations.short: The actor surrogate combining return maximization and entropy exploration.
annotations.details: The first term is $\log\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)$ weighted by normalized advantage; the second is $\eta$-scaled policy entropy. The loss is minimized over actor parameters $\theta$.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{sg}(R_t^\lambda-v_\psi(s_t))/\max(1,S)$
annotations.short: The stopped advantage $\sg(R_t^\lambda-v_\psi(s_t))/\max(1,S)$.
annotations.details: $R_t^\lambda-v_\psi(s_t)$ measures whether an imagined outcome exceeds the critic baseline. The robust denominator compares scales without magnifying small noisy returns.

annotations.label: $\mathrm H[\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)]$
annotations.short: The entropy of the actor's action distribution at a state.
annotations.details: Higher $\mathrm H[\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)]$ indicates a less concentrated policy and encourages exploration. Its coefficient $\eta$ is fixed across domains.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{EMA}(\operatorname{Per}_{95}-\operatorname{Per}_{5})$
annotations.short: An exponential moving average of the 95th-to-5th percentile return span.
annotations.details: Percentiles reduce sensitivity to outliers, and EMA coefficient $0.99$ smooths batch changes. The result is actor return scale $S$.

annotations.label: Symlog squared error
annotations.short: Squared error applied after compressing targets with the symmetric logarithm.
annotations.details: The network predicts $\symlog(y)$, and $\symexp$ maps its output back to the original scale. This reduces gradient sensitivity to magnitude while supporting negative values.

annotations.label: $f(x,\theta)$
annotations.short: A neural-network output in transformed target space.
annotations.details: For deterministic regression, $f(x,\theta)$ approximates $\symlog(y)$; for categorical regression it supplies logits. $\theta$ denotes the prediction-network parameters.

annotations.label: $y$
annotations.short: A scalar prediction target such as an observation component, reward, or return.
annotations.details: Its physical scale depends on the application domain and may span orders of magnitude. The symlog transformation and two-hot encoding make learning less sensitive to that scale.

annotations.label: $\hat y$
annotations.short: The symlog-regression prediction $\hat y$ on the original target scale.
annotations.details: Here $\hat y\doteq\symexp(f(x,\theta))$. Applying symexp, the inverse function of symlog, restores the units and scale of target $y$.

annotations.label: $\hat y$
annotations.short: The categorical-bin prediction $\hat y$ on the original target scale.
annotations.details: Here $\hat y\doteq\softmax(f(x))^\mathsf T B$, the probability-weighted mean of symexp-spaced bins. Its units match target $y$.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L$
annotations.short: Half the squared difference between network output and symlog-transformed target.
annotations.details: The transformation compresses large magnitudes before squared error is applied. Prediction is decoded by applying symexp, the inverse function of symlog.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{symlog}$
annotations.details: Dreamer applies symlog to vector observations and regression targets so that very different numerical scales can share one learning configuration.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{symexp}$
annotations.details: Dreamer uses symexp to restore symlog predictions to their original scale and to construct signed support bins spanning many orders of magnitude.

annotations.label: Symexp twohot loss
annotations.short: Categorical prediction over symexp-spaced bins using two-bin soft targets.
annotations.details: The critic and reward head use this method for possibly stochastic targets. It decouples gradient scale from numerical target magnitude while retaining continuous-valued readouts.

annotations.label: $B=\{b_i\}$
annotations.short: The set of symexp-spaced scalar support bins and its individual locations.
annotations.details: $B$ is obtained by applying $\symexp$ to values evenly spaced from $-20$ to $+20$. Probability-weighted averaging over $B$ produces continuous prediction $\hat y$.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{softmax}(f(x))$
annotations.details: In Dreamer's reward and critic heads, softmax converts network logits $f(x)$ into probabilities over bin set $B$. Their inner product with $B$ is the scalar prediction $\hat y$.

annotations.label: $\mathcal L$
annotations.short: Cross entropy between the twohot target and predicted log-softmax probabilities.
annotations.details: The loss depends on assigned bin probabilities rather than the numerical size of bin locations. This helps stabilize reward and return prediction across domains.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{log\,softmax}(f(x,\theta))$
annotations.short: Log probabilities obtained by normalizing the network logits.
annotations.details: Taking the inner product with $\twohot(y)$ selects an interpolated categorical log likelihood. The negative of that quantity is minimized.

annotations.label: CNN
annotations.details: Dreamer's encoder and decoder use CNNs for image observations.

annotations.label: MLP
annotations.details: Dreamer uses MLPs for vector encoders and decoders, the actor and critic, and the dynamics, reward, and continuation predictors.

annotations.label: Latent categorical distributions
annotations.short: Each discrete latent factor is sampled from probabilities produced by softmax.
annotations.details: Dreamer represents the stochastic state as a vector of categorical variables. The 1% uniform mixture prevents any category from receiving exactly zero probability, while the straight-through estimator carries learning signals through samples.

annotations.label: $\phi$
annotations.short: $\phi$ denotes the collective trainable parameters of the world-model components.
annotations.details: These parameters govern the encoder, recurrent transition, latent dynamics, reward and continuation predictors, and decoder. The objective $\mathcal L(\phi)$ updates them jointly.

annotations.label: $\operatorname E$
annotations.details: Dreamer uses expectation to average the world-model loss over encoder samples and to read a scalar value from the critic's categorical return distribution.

annotations.label: $\psi$
annotations.short: $\psi$ denotes the critic network's trainable parameters.
annotations.details: They determine the categorical return distribution $v_\psi(R_t\mid s_t)$ and are optimized by the critic negative-log-likelihood objective.

annotations.label: $\theta$
annotations.short: $\theta$ denotes the actor policy's trainable parameters in the actor objective.
annotations.details: They govern $\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)$ and receive gradients from the normalized REINFORCE term and the entropy bonus. This role is distinct from the later reuse of $\theta$ for a generic prediction network.

annotations.label: $\theta$
annotations.short: $\theta$ denotes the generic prediction network's parameters in the robust-prediction subsection.
annotations.details: Here it parameterizes $f(x,\theta)$ for symlog or twohot prediction. It is a local reuse of the glyph $\theta$, not the actor-specific parameter role used in the preceding subsection.

annotations.label: Normal distribution
annotations.details: The paper considers a Normal critic as a simple alternative, but uses a categorical critic because return distributions may be multimodal and vary greatly in scale.

annotations.label: Categorical critic distribution
annotations.short: Dreamer's critic represents return uncertainty with probabilities over a finite set of transformed bins.
annotations.details: Unlike a single Normal density, this finite categorical representation can express multiple modes. Symexp-spaced bin locations cover returns with widely different magnitudes.

annotations.label: PPO
annotations.details: The paper evaluates Dreamer against a strong PPO implementation configured with one fixed hyperparameter setting across domains.

annotations.label: Replay ratio
annotations.short: The replay ratio measures how many training time steps are consumed per newly collected environment time step, before accounting for action repeat.
annotations.details: Dividing the replay ratio by the total time steps in a minibatch (batch size times sequence length) and by action repeat gives the number of parameter-update steps per environment step. It controls the trade-off between computation and data efficiency.

annotations.label: AGC
annotations.details: Dreamer clips each tensor's gradient when its norm exceeds $30\%$ of the corresponding weight norm, using $\epsilon=10^{-3}$ to handle very small weights.

annotations.label: L2 norm
annotations.details: Dreamer's adaptive gradient clipping compares each tensor's gradient norm with the L2 norm of its corresponding weight tensor.

annotations.label: LaProp
annotations.details: Dreamer uses LaProp with numerical-stability constant $\epsilon=10^{-20}$; the paper reports that its normalize-then-momentum ordering avoids occasional instabilities observed with Adam.

annotations.label: RMSProp
annotations.details: In Dreamer's optimizer, LaProp applies RMSProp-style gradient normalization before momentum smoothing.

annotations.label: Adam
annotations.details: The paper contrasts Adam's raw-gradient moment accumulation with LaProp's normalize-then-momentum ordering and reports occasional instability under Adam.

annotations.label: One-percent uniform mixture
annotations.short: Dreamer mixes the encoder, dynamics-predictor, and categorical actor probabilities with 1% uniform probability mass.
annotations.details: For $K$ categories, Dreamer replaces each predicted probability $p_i$ by $p'_i=0.99p_i+0.01/K$. Therefore no category can receive zero probability, sampled categories retain finite log probabilities, and the latent KL terms remain bounded.

annotations.label: $i$
annotations.short: $i$ selects one component of the twohot target vector.
annotations.details: Only components at the neighboring-bin indices $k$ and $k+1$ are nonzero; all other components are zero.

annotations.label: $k$
annotations.short: $k$ indexes the bin immediately below the scalar target $x$.
annotations.details: The indicator sum counts bin locations smaller than $x$. The twohot interpolation then assigns mass to bins $b_k$ and $b_{k+1}$.

annotations.label: $\operatorname{\delta}(b_j<x)$
annotations.details: In the two-hot definition, summing $\operatorname{\delta}(b_j<x)$ counts the support bins strictly below target $x$ and determines neighboring-bin index $k$.

annotations.label: GRU
annotations.details: Dreamer's sequence model uses a block-structured GRU whose recurrent weights are split into eight blocks, reducing parameter and compute growth while retaining cross-block mixing through its inputs.

annotations.label: KL balance
annotations.short: KL balance uses two differently stopped KL terms to control learning pressure on the latent predictor and encoder.
annotations.details: The dynamics loss updates the predictor toward a stopped encoder target, while the representation loss updates the encoder toward a stopped predictor. Separate global weights let Dreamer favor predictive dynamics without collapsing informative representations.

KL.short: The Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence $\mathrm{KL}(q\,\|\,p)=\mathbb E_q[\log q-\log p]$ measures how much one distribution differs from another.
KL.details: It is nonnegative and equals zero only when the two distributions coincide; it is not symmetric. Optimizing a KL term pulls one distribution toward the other, and which side receives the stop-gradient decides which network learns.

NLL.short: The negative log likelihood $-\ln p(y)$ scores how surprising an outcome $y$ is under a model.
NLL.details: Minimizing summed negative log likelihoods is maximum-likelihood training: it pushes probability mass toward observed targets. Lower values mean the model assigns higher probability to the data.

Entropy.short: Entropy measures how spread out a distribution is: for discrete actions, $\mathrm H[P]=-\sum_a P(a)\log P(a)$; for a continuous action density $p(a)$, differential entropy is $\mathrm H[p]=-\int p(a)\log p(a)\,da$.
Entropy.details: Here $a$ denotes an outcome, $P(a)$ is its probability in the discrete case, and $p(a)$ is its probability density in the continuous case. Higher entropy generally indicates a less concentrated distribution.

EMA.short: An exponential moving average (EMA) with decay $\rho$ updates a running estimate as $\bar x\leftarrow\rho\bar x+(1-\rho)x$.
EMA.details: A decay $\rho$ near one gives more weight to the previous estimate and less to the newest observation, smoothing noisy measurements into a stable running statistic.

REINFORCE.short: REINFORCE is a score-function gradient estimator: $\nabla_\theta\,\mathbb E[R]\approx\mathbb E[\sg(R)\,\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(a)]$.
REINFORCE.details: It weights the log probability of sampled actions by the observed return or advantage. The weighting term uses a stop-gradient so gradients flow only through the log-probability factor.

Categorical.short: A categorical distribution is a discrete probability distribution on a finite support of $K$ outcomes.
Categorical.details: For support $\{1,\ldots,K\}$ and category probabilities $p_1,\ldots,p_K$ satisfying $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^K p_i=1$, its probability mass function is $\Pr(X=i)=p_i$. Neural networks commonly obtain these probabilities from logits using softmax.

Bernoulli.short: A Bernoulli distribution is a discrete probability distribution on the binary support $\{0,1\}$.
Bernoulli.details: With success probability $p\in[0,1]$, its probability mass function is $\Pr(X=x)=p^x(1-p)^{1-x}$ for $x\in\{0,1\}$. Its negative log likelihood is binary cross-entropy.

Softmax.short: The softmax function converts real-valued logits $f_i$ into probabilities $\softmax(f)_i=e^{f_i}/\sum_j e^{f_j}$.
Softmax.details: It produces nonnegative weights summing to one over bins or classes. Its logarithm, log-softmax, is numerically stable and appears directly in cross-entropy losses.

Percentile.short: The $q$th percentile is the value below which approximately $q$ percent of samples fall.
Percentile.details: Ranges such as the 95th-minus-5th percentile measure spread while ignoring extreme outliers, giving robust scale estimates.

Gradient.short: The gradient $\nabla$ collects partial derivatives and points in the direction of steepest increase.
Gradient.details: A stop-gradient operation returns its input unchanged in the forward pass but blocks gradient flow backward, treating part of the computation as a fixed constant.

Expectation.short: Expectation is the probability-weighted average value of a random variable.
Expectation.details: For discrete outcomes it is a probability-weighted sum; for continuous outcomes it is a density-weighted integral.

ModelBasedRL.label: Model-based reinforcement learning
ModelBasedRL.short: Model-based reinforcement learning learns or uses a model of environment dynamics to improve decisions.
ModelBasedRL.details: The learned model can support planning or generate simulated experience, reducing the need for direct interaction with the real environment.

WorldModel.label: World model
WorldModel.short: A world model predicts how an environment evolves and what outcomes actions produce.
WorldModel.details: A latent world model compresses observations into internal states before predicting transitions, rewards, and termination. This allows behavior learning to operate on compact imagined trajectories.

RSSM.label: Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM)
RSSM.short: An RSSM combines deterministic recurrent memory with stochastic latent state variables.
RSSM.details: The recurrent component carries history, while stochastic states represent uncertainty and new information from observations.

CNN.label: Convolutional neural network (CNN)
CNN.short: A CNN processes grid-structured data such as images using shared local filters.
CNN.details: Weight sharing makes convolutional layers efficient and translation-aware.

MLP.label: Multilayer perceptron (MLP)
MLP.short: An MLP is a feed-forward neural network composed of stacked affine layers and nonlinear activations.
MLP.details: Each layer transforms its input with learned weights and biases, usually followed by a nonlinear activation except at the output.

Normal.label: Normal distribution
Normal.short: The Normal distribution is a continuous probability distribution on the real line.
Normal.details: With mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma>0$, its support is $x\in\mathbb R$ and its density is $f_X(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)$. A single Normal density is unimodal.

NormalParameters.label: Normal-distribution parameters
NormalParameters.short: In a Normal density, $\mu$ is the mean, $\sigma$ is the positive standard deviation, and $x$ is the real-valued outcome.
NormalParameters.details: The constant $\pi$ is the circle constant and $\exp$ is the exponential function. The variance is $\sigma^2$.

CategoryProbabilities.label: Categorical-probability notation
CategoryProbabilities.short: $K$ is the number of categories, $i$ is a category index, and $p_i$ is the probability assigned to category $i$.
CategoryProbabilities.details: The probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one. $X$ denotes the sampled categorical random variable.

BernoulliParameter.label: Bernoulli-distribution notation
BernoulliParameter.short: $p$ is the probability of outcome $1$, $X$ is the binary random variable, and $x$ is one realized value in $\{0,1\}$.
BernoulliParameter.details: The complementary probability of outcome $0$ is $1-p$.

Logits.short: Logits are unconstrained real-valued scores that softmax converts into probabilities.
Logits.details: Adding the same constant to every logit leaves softmax probabilities unchanged; differences between logits determine relative probability ratios.

PercentileLevel.label: Percentile level
PercentileLevel.short: The symbol $q$ specifies the requested percentile or quantile level.
PercentileLevel.details: Depending on convention it is written as a fraction from zero to one or as a percentage from zero to one hundred.

PolicyGradient.label: Policy gradient
PolicyGradient.short: A policy gradient differentiates expected return with respect to the parameters of a stochastic policy.
PolicyGradient.details: Score-function estimators such as REINFORCE use gradients of sampled-action log probabilities, weighted by returns or advantages.

PPO.label: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
PPO.short: PPO is an on-policy reinforcement-learning algorithm that limits how much the policy changes during an update.
PPO.details: It optimizes a clipped policy-gradient surrogate over recently collected trajectories, discouraging destabilizingly large policy updates.

AGC.label: Adaptive Gradient Clipping (AGC)
AGC.short: AGC clips a parameter tensor's gradient relative to the norm of that parameter tensor.
AGC.details: Its threshold adapts to parameter scale, reducing sensitivity to the absolute scale of losses and helping prevent destabilizing updates.

L2Norm.label: L2 norm
L2Norm.short: The L2 norm is the square root of the sum of squared components of a vector or flattened tensor.
L2Norm.details: It measures Euclidean magnitude and is invariant under rotations and reflections.

LaProp.short: LaProp is an adaptive optimizer that applies RMS-style gradient normalization before momentum.
LaProp.details: This ordering differs from Adam, which accumulates first- and second-moment estimates from raw gradients.

RMSProp.short: RMSProp rescales gradients using an exponential moving average of their squared magnitudes.
RMSProp.details: Coordinates with persistently large gradients receive smaller effective steps.

Adam.short: Adam is an adaptive optimizer combining momentum-like first moments with second-moment gradient scaling.
Adam.details: Bias-corrected running estimates determine coordinate-wise update sizes.

DiscreteUniform.label: Discrete uniform distribution
DiscreteUniform.short: A discrete uniform distribution assigns equal probability to every outcome in a finite support.
DiscreteUniform.details: For support $\{1,\ldots,K\}$, its probability mass function is $\Pr(X=i)=1/K$ for every $i$ in the support and zero otherwise.

Indicator.label: Indicator function
Indicator.short: An indicator function evaluates to one when its condition is true and zero otherwise.
Indicator.details: Summing indicators counts how many indexed conditions hold.

GRU.label: Gated recurrent unit (GRU)
GRU.short: A GRU is a recurrent neural-network cell with gates that control memory updates.
GRU.details: Update and reset gates help it retain useful information across long sequences.

ActorCritic.label: Actor-critic reinforcement learning
ActorCritic.short: Actor-critic methods pair an action-selection policy with a value estimator that evaluates the policy's outcomes.
ActorCritic.details: The actor adjusts behavior using signals derived from the critic, while the critic learns return estimates.

Policy.label: Policy
Policy.short: A policy is a conditional rule or probability distribution for selecting actions from states.
Policy.details: A stochastic policy assigns probabilities or densities to available actions. Its trainable parameters determine how action selection changes with state.

LogisticRegression.label: Logistic regression
LogisticRegression.short: Logistic regression models a binary outcome using a sigmoid-transformed real-valued score.
LogisticRegression.details: It is trained with Bernoulli negative log likelihood, also called binary cross-entropy.

StopGradient.label: Stop-gradient operator
StopGradient.short: A stop-gradient operator returns the same numerical value but has zero derivative.
StopGradient.details: It makes its argument behave as a fixed target during backpropagation.

Symlog.label: Symmetric logarithm (symlog)
Symlog.details: It behaves approximately linearly near zero and logarithmically at large magnitudes, supporting both positive and negative targets. Its inverse function is symexp: $\operatorname{symexp}(\operatorname{symlog}(x))=x$.

Symexp.label: Symmetric exponential (symexp)
Symexp.short: Symexp is the inverse function of symlog: $\operatorname{symexp}(x)=\operatorname{sign}(x)(\exp(|x|)-1)$.
Symexp.details: It satisfies $\operatorname{symexp}(\operatorname{symlog}(y))=y$ and maps uniformly spaced transformed coordinates to signed values whose magnitudes grow exponentially.

Twohot.label: Two-hot encoding
Twohot.short: A two-hot encoding represents a continuous-valued scalar using a discrete categorical distribution over fixed support bins, splitting its target probability between the two neighboring bins.
Twohot.details: For a scalar target $y$ lying between adjacent bins $b_i \le y \le b_{i+1}$, two-hot encoding assigns weights $w_i=(b_{i+1}-y)/(b_{i+1}-b_i)$ and $w_{i+1}=(y-b_i)/(b_{i+1}-b_i)$, with all other entries zero. Thus, although $y$ is continuous-valued, its training representation is a discrete distribution over the finite bin set. The weights sum to one and satisfy $w_i b_i+w_{i+1}b_{i+1}=y$, preserving the scalar through interpolation instead of snapping it to one bin. The network may predict probability on all bins and is trained with cross entropy against this two-bin target. At inference, the continuous-valued prediction is recovered as the probability-weighted average over all bin values. This combines continuous-valued prediction with the stable gradients of categorical learning.

RMSNorm.label: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization (RMSNorm)
RMSNorm.short: RMSNorm rescales a feature vector by its root-mean-square magnitude.
RMSNorm.details: Unlike LayerNorm, it does not subtract the feature mean. Learned scale parameters restore per-feature flexibility after normalization.

SiLU.label: Sigmoid Linear Unit (SiLU)
SiLU.details: Multiplying the input by its sigmoid gate yields a smooth, non-monotone activation also known as swish.

Sigmoid.label: Logistic sigmoid
Sigmoid.short: The sigmoid function maps a real input $x$ to $\sigma(x)=1/(1+e^{-x})$ in the open interval from zero to one.
Sigmoid.details: It is commonly used as a gate or to parameterize the success probability of a Bernoulli distribution.
